title: Computer Engineering, B.S. (Behrend)
notes: Penn State Erie, The Behrend College -- a genuinely separate curriculum from University Park's Computer Engineering, B.S. (CMPEN-2026.json), confirmed by direct bulletin comparison 2026-08-27: Behrend's own required CMPEN sequence (CMPEN 351, 371, 352W, 411, 441, 461, 480, 481) shares only CMPEN 431 with UP's own required set (CMPEN 270, 331, 362, 431, 482W) -- Behrend runs its own ABET-accredited computer engineering curriculum, not a 2+2 feeder. Built fresh (Pattern B) as CMPENBH per this session's new-major-code convention (UP code CMPEN + 'BH'). Real 8-semester Suggested Academic Plan, 129 total credits, taken verbatim from the live 2026-27 Behrend bulletin page. The bulletin's second-year Fall item 'CMPEN 270 or 271 & 275' is modeled as CMPEN 271 + CMPEN 275 (two separate real items, 3cr+1cr=4cr, matching the bulletin's combined 4cr line) rather than CMPEN 270: cmpen_catalog.json's own real prereq_groups for every downstream Behrend-required course in this plan (CMPEN 351, 371, 411, 461) name CMPEN 271 and/or CMPEN 275 specifically, never CMPEN 270 -- the reverse of UP's own CMPEN-2026 choice (which picked plain CMPEN 270 because UP's own downstream courses, CMPEN 331/431, only ever name 270). 'Technical Elective (300/400-level)' (x4, Semesters 7-8) is wired to the bulletin's own Primary/Secondary Technical Elective structure via a merged match pool (any 300-400 SWENG/EE/CMPEN course, any 400-level CMPSC course except 455/456, plus the enumerated Secondary list) -- the real 'at least 2 primary, at most 1 secondary' ratio isn't independently enforceable by this engine's plain match mechanism, documented as an approximation, not fabricated. Real-prereq-chain fixes (same pattern as CMPEN-2026/EMET-2026): (1) CHEM 110 -> MATH 22 -> MATH 21 -- added MATH 21 + MATH 22 (Semester 1) since neither was natively in this plan's sequence. (2) CMPSC 121 (the plan's own explicitly-required intro course, not the more flexible UP-style 'CMPSC 121 or 131' pool) has a real prereq of MATH 110 (math_catalog.json), which itself needs MATH 22 or MATH 41 -- added MATH 110 (Semester 1, after MATH 22) so CMPSC 121 -> CMPSC 122's real chain (CMPSC 122's only real prereq is literally CMPSC 121, no 131/201 alternate) actually unlocks. This placement-ladder detour (MATH 21 -> 22 -> 110 -> CMPSC 121 -> 122) costs real simulated terms and is the same kind of gap EMET-2026's own notes flag for MATH 110/CMPSC 121; verified via build_full_plan that it produces zero 'Could not schedule' failures, only the same routine 1-extra-term overtime warning every other major's plan produces under today's real simulation clock (confirmed by re-running ME-2026 itself, which shows the identical single-extra-term warning).
